candidate_diagrams.claim: At a two-point boundary law, allowed DQM scores form the ray {aX:a≥0}, while the closed linear tangent space is all of L²₀(P₀)={bX:b∈R}.
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The example explicitly distinguishes a nonlinear half-line of admissible scores from its linear span, so a small geometric sketch can make the distinction immediate.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: Draw score coordinate bX horizontally: highlight the nonnegative ray as the score cone, the full real line as L²₀(P₀), mark 0 and X, and show −X lies in the tangent space but outside the score cone. Label these as subsets of the one-dimensional mean-zero space.

candidate_diagrams.claim: For testing μ≤0 at μ=0 in the unit-variance normal location model, the local null is a half-line and the likelihood-ratio limit is (G∨0)² with law ½χ²₀+½χ²₁.
candidate_diagrams.kind: local parameter cone and chi-bar-square distribution sketch
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The item ties a one-sided local constraint to projection onto a half-line and an atom at zero; an annotated one-dimensional geometric sketch would connect the boundary geometry to the mixture law.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: Draw the local parameter axis h with full model R and null cone (−∞,0]; show the Gaussian score G, its projection onto the null cone, and the squared distance giving (G∨0)². Beside it show a mass 1/2 at zero and a 1/2 χ²₁ component. Mark the graphic as explanatory for this example.
candidate_diagrams.confidence: possible, source-supported; keep the sign convention aligned with h≤0 and do not imply an exact finite-sample chi-square law

candidate_diagrams.claim: Orthogonal decomposition of the observation space separates fitted and residual Gaussian coordinates; for nested designs it splits residual coordinates into the reduced-model increment and full-model residual, yielding independent chi-square sums and exact t/F pivots.
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The proof repeatedly uses a geometric orthogonal decomposition and independent coordinate blocks to explain the exact distributions; a diagram can clarify the roles of the fitted space and the two residual subspaces.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: Show Rⁿ=W_R⊕W_D⊕W_U⊥ with W_D=W_U∩W_R⊥, dimensions p−q, q, n−p; indicate projected Gaussian components and independent squared norms RSS_R−RSS_U=σ²χ²_q and RSS_U=σ²χ²_{n−p}. For the one-model t pivot, separately label col(X) and col(X)⊥ with p and n−p dimensions. Do not suggest randomness in the deterministic subspaces.
